study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals were used to identify extreme functional connections. The tolerance package in R was used to estimate 90% tolerance proportion with 10% confidence level for each functional connection in healthy controls. This approach identifies individual-level abnormalities by comparing against normative ranges derived from healthy controls.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we used the 'tolerance' package in R (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tolerance/tolerance.pdf) to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs. Following prior studies, we set a 90% tolerance proportion with a 10% confidence level
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Fang2025.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Identifying extreme functional connections in MDD

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Resting-state functional connectivity was computed as pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients between regional signals from 200 brain regions (Craddock 200 atlas), Fisher Z-transformed. This produced a 200x200 functional connectivity matrix for each participant.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Functional networks were estimated by calculating pairwise Pearson's correlation coefficients between regional signals, with the resulting values transformed to Fisher Z scores. This procedure produced a 200 x 200 functional connectivity matrix for each participant.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Fang2025.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Functional connectivity features and harmonization

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model (tolerance interval estimation) did not include explicit explanatory variables. Tolerance intervals were computed directly from healthy control functional connectivity values without regression on covariates. However, Combat harmonization was applied to remove site effects prior to tolerance interval computation, and subsequent group comparison analyses controlled for sex, age, study site, and mean framewise displacement (head motion).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we used the 'tolerance' package in R to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs; we applied the Combat method to harmonize the functional connections across these sites
